spontaneous_story_understanding: The story explains a general COVID lockdown demand collapse and oil glut, plus a specific delivery and storage problem for WTI at Cushing as the May futures contract approached expiry. Traders unable to accept physical oil paid others to take their contracts. Brent also suffered from the glut but, according to the prose, its different settlement arrangement avoided this particular obligation. The negative daily spot quote lasted one day and did not make weekly or monthly averages negative.
what_prose_adds_or_changes: My chart-first reading of a shared decline plus a WTI-specific daily exception remains intact. Prose supplies the meaning of negative prices, expands WTI and identifies its location, identifies Brent and its transport context, supplies EIA provenance, and distinguishes the minus $36.98 spot figure from the minus $37.63 futures settlement. It also adds historical counts and claims of uniqueness beyond the chart window. It answers the causal question with attributed external explanations while expressly saying that the plotted dataset cannot test causation.
prose_chart_relationship: Chart 1 makes the shared fall and exceptionally sharp WTI break visible; the text gives the event a location and proposed mechanism. Brent nearly catches down to WTI the following day, so the text prevents the reader treating Brent as unaffected. Chart 2 supports the limited meaning of the sensational daily number: the broader averages remain positive. The charts do not independently support the storage, liquidity, demand, futures mechanics or historical uniqueness claims.
uncertainty_and_unanswered_questions: The mechanism is described through expiring futures contracts, whereas the chart and opening statement concern a spot quote. The prose distinguishes the two numbers but does not fully explain how futures distress produces that particular spot quote.
I still do not know how full storage was, what made available storage inaccessible to those traders, or what low liquidity means in practical terms here.
The title says one place, while the displayed evidence compares two benchmarks. I read the place as Cushing, but the charts cannot establish an exhaustive worldwide claim.
The historical counts and assertions about no other negative averages extend beyond the displayed dates; I have not verified them.
The averaging procedure and treatment of days without quotes remain unspecified.
presentation_observations: The title appears twice consecutively in story.md. Text and chart labels are readable. Source and build links are present but were not followed.
